requirements.requirement: Every sudo-executed command on node1 is logged with the acting user and timestamp to /var/log/sudo-commands.log
requirements.summary: A dedicated /etc/sudoers.d/99-sudo-logfile Defaults block (logfile="/var/log/sudo-commands.log", log_year) was validated with visudo and installed. Captured log entries show full-year timestamps, the acting user (root and a disposable test user sudologtest), and the executed command for multiple invocations both before and after a reboot.

requirements.requirement: Sudo command entries are kept out of the general system log (auth.log/syslog)
requirements.summary: Defaults !syslog was added alongside the dedicated logfile directive. COMMAND= line counts in /var/log/auth.log stayed frozen at 7 (all pre-dating the change) across multiple subsequent sudo invocations both before and after reboot, and /var/log/syslog showed zero COMMAND= entries throughout, while the dedicated log file kept accumulating new entries.

requirements.requirement: Correct attribution for non-root sudo users
requirements.summary: A disposable NOPASSWD test user (sudologtest) was created, ran a sudo command, and the dedicated log correctly recorded 'sudologtest' as the acting user with USER=root as the target; the temporary user and its sudoers file were then fully removed.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol: healthy baseline, restart, changed boot identity, and recovered service/data state on node1
requirements.summary: Pre-restart baseline captured boot_id, uptime, active rsyslog, sudoers config, and 24-line log (cmd-abf900704e5d4e4b), matching the fixed before_prepare boot-identity snapshot. A backgrounded 'shutdown -r now' was issued and acknowledged, an immediate follow-up probe failed with connection reset confirming the node went down, and the subsequent boot_id read differently, matching the fixed after_executor snapshot. Post-restart checks confirmed rsyslog active, sudoers config intact, the log file persisted with prior entries plus new appended lines, and a fresh sudo command continued to log exclusively to the dedicated file with no new auth.log COMMAND= entries.

overall_summary: The executor correctly configured node1 so sudo command executions are logged with user and full-year timestamp to /var/log/sudo-commands.log via a validated sudoers Defaults drop-in, and disabled sudo's syslog output so entries no longer reach auth.log/syslog (confirmed by frozen/zero COMMAND= counts across multiple invocations). Attribution was verified for both root and a disposable non-root test user, which was cleanly removed afterward. The mandatory node-restart evidence protocol was fully executed and observed: a healthy pre-restart baseline, a real disruption (connection reset), a distinct post-restart boot identity matching the fixed lifecycle snapshots, and confirmed recovery of the logging configuration, log file continuity, and exclusive-logging behavior post-reboot. No unnecessary or unreverted mutations were found.
limitations: No independent evidence beyond the executor's own commands (e.g., no evaluator-side log inspection) was available; all conclusions rely on the captured command outputs.

PAM session-open/close messages from sudo continue to appear in auth.log even after !syslog was set, but these are unrelated to sudo's own command logging and do not conflict with the task's 'commands run through sudo' scope.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing commands map clearly to the task: creating and permissioning the log file, writing/validating/installing the sudoers Defaults drop-in, and a bounded verification cycle using a temporary NOPASSWD test user (sudologtest) and its temporary sudoers file, both of which were fully removed afterward (cmd-f80e01a6039944bf). The lifecycle diff confirms no residual temp files, failed services, or unexpected listening sockets attributable to the executor beyond expected reboot-related ephemeral systemd-private directories. The only anomaly, 'userdel: mail spool not found', is a harmless informational message from removing a home-dir-only test account, not a hygiene issue. The reboot itself (cmd-54358a65131c4518) was a required, single, bounded mutation directly tied to the mandatory restart-evidence protocol.
